primary_task: Harden PowerShell automation and Windows endpoint configuration against a security baseline, with logging, execution policy and JEA-restricted remoting enabled and verified.

requirements.name: windows endpoints
requirements.evidence: You are a PowerShell and Windows security hardening specialist ... Harden scheduled tasks, WinRM endpoints, and service accounts; PowerShell logging enabled and verified; Remoting restricted using JEA or custom endpoints
requirements.basis: lacks: "Windows or macOS, and their GUI toolchains (Xcode, Visual Studio, PowerShell on Windows)"

requirements.name: powershell/pwsh
requirements.evidence: Apply CIS / DISA STIG controls using PowerShell; Validate Execution Policy, Code Signing

requirements.name: Key Vault / SecretManagement
requirements.evidence: Implement secure credential patterns (SecretManagement, Key Vault, DPAPI, Credential Locker)
requirements.basis: lacks: "connectors or integrations other than the tools listed"

requirements.name: read/grep/edit
requirements.evidence: tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep; Review modules/scripts for least privilege design; Detect anti-patterns (embedded passwords, plain-text creds, insecure logs)
requirements.basis: tools.read: "read files in the working directory; search them by name pattern or content (glob, grep)"; tools.edit: "edit existing files and Jupyter notebooks"

notes: Two readings. (a) Taken here: hardening means applying and verifying controls (logging 'enabled and verified', remoting restricted, CIS/STIG applied), which needs Windows endpoints and PowerShell, both unavailable. (b) If the request is only a static code review of .ps1 files in the repo for anti-patterns (plaintext creds, Write-Host leaking secrets), it can be done with read/grep/edit and the verdict would be ACHIEVABLE.
